summary:
The Matrix Moon web application was developed to provide precise and advanced geographical, topographical, and environmental analyses for five strategic lunar sites, including historical landing locations and complex polar regions such as Shackleton Crater.

**How does the project address the challenge?**
The system processes spatial data and digital elevation models derived from NASA resources, while integrating machine learning algorithms using Python (`Scikit-learn` and `NumPy`) to calculate slope angles, thermal ranges, and solar illumination rates with high accuracy, effectively streamlining topographical risk assessments for landing sites.

**Why is it important?**
The project plays a vital role in supporting future space exploration missions. It provides researchers and engineers with a reliable tool to select the safest and most sustainable locations for spacecraft, directly contributing to the success and efficiency of crewed and robotic lunar missions.
details:
Project Details

  • What it does and how it works: It is an integrated web application called Lunar Landing Site Navigator that performs precise geographical, topographical, and environmental analyses of strategic lunar landing sites (such as Apollo 11, Apollo 17, Chang'e 4, Chandrayaan-3, and Shackleton Crater). It works by gathering and processing spatial digital data—such as elevation files (LDEM/DEM) and machine learning algorithms via embedded Python scripts—to calculate elevations, slope angles, thermal radiation, and illumination rates.
  • Its benefits: It provides accurate readings on elevation gradients and surface slopes to assess landing safety for future spacecraft, and assists researchers in selecting sites with an optimal balance of power, solar illumination, and topography.
  • The desired impact: It enriches space research by bridging the gap between software models, machine learning, and geospatial space data (GIS) within a unified web environment, supporting safer future lunar exploration missions.
    • Programming Languages: Python.
    • Frameworks & Libraries: Flask (backend framework), Gunicorn (web server), NumPy & Scikit-learn (data analysis and machine learning).
    • Frontend Technologies: HTML and JavaScript for the interactive interface and map browsing (index.html).
    • Data & GIS Files: Standard lunar elevation models (LDEM_4.LBL) and machine learning reports (ml_report.json).
    • Hardware: A high-performance laptop with a touchscreen display to handle spatial browsing and layer analysis efficiently.
  • The creative aspect: It combines multi-layered spatial analysis—linking factors like elevation, slope, thermal max, and solar illumination—with automated site suitability evaluation using custom machine learning training tools (train_suitability.py), managing the massive contrast between smooth equatorial maria and complex polar slopes.
  • Factors considered by the team: Accounting for severe topographical and latitudinal constraints (such as polar vs. equatorial differences), ensuring accurate geospatial standards to prevent data reading errors, and maintaining high compatibility for spatial data exporting.
